items.title: Player interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2012
items.q: my idol was Ray Brown. I still listen to him and I hear his sound and go wow man, I try to play like that.

ctx.x: That was a great thing you just said. I really enjoyed hearing you say it. And it’s interesting too, sometimes you make an impression on young people too, that you don’t know you’re doing it. And I’ve had instances around here, like 25, 30 years later, some adult comes up to me and says, “do you remember that time,” and there were some kids yesterday who was really — and so you just never know.

I talked this morning to Hank, and that’s what I said to him this morning. You know he was getting up, getting ready to go to work, and I was up having some coffee, I woke up early this morning. And while he was going on, he said, “was everything okay yesterday? How did you feel about it?” “Oh, it was great.” It was like, “did you see those kids © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

dancing and moving around?” I said, “yeah, man.” I said, “that’s Louis Armstrong right there.” You know, because, and the reason why say it is because he was saying this particular group of kids were like from, there were some kids that were supposed to be like troubled kids or something like that, I’m not sure about that. And I told him, I said, “oh yeah, put a horn in their hand.” But that’s how it starts, you know. I was an average student in school. I mean I probably could have done a lot better — I’m more…
